baseline_models.focus_anchor: يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ ... مِنْ عَاصِمٍ ... مِنْ هَادٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: A severe event becomes a rout: doubled back-turning removes both protection from harm and orientation toward a viable direction.

activation_trace.role: The branch's severe event gives the temporal frame the pressure of a crisis rather than a neutral date.
Turning away supplies the first act of retreat and relational disengagement.
Presenting the back in flight intensifies the retreat into exposed rout.
Preventive holding and preservation supplies the protection explicitly absent.
Deviation from intended direction explains why movement does not become escape.
Gentle indication toward a true road supplies the orienting function explicitly absent.

changed_reading.before: The ayah says that people flee on judgment day and have no savior or guide.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an exposed rout in which rapid movement, loss of protection, and loss of direction form one failed-escape mechanism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ followed by the negated عَاصِم and هَاد
baseline_models.mechanism: The same focus root that can image proximity, guardianship, and support is realized as turning away; the doubled retreat therefore reads as a reversal of sustaining relation, not locomotion alone.

activation_trace.role: Nearness without an interval supplies the relational state that the enacted turning reverses.
Alliance and support make the lost proximity specifically protective rather than merely spatial.
The actual verbal branch selects withdrawal and rejection from among those relational possibilities.
Mutual back-turning and estrangement extends the bodily posture into severed social relation.
Protective holding names the relational function no longer available after the reversal.

changed_reading.before: Turning the back is simply the visible posture of fugitives.
changed_reading.after: Turning the back enacts a reversal from proximity and protective alliance into estrangement, after which neither holding protection nor orientation remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah places formally parallel claims to guide toward the path of right in Pharaoh's mouth and the believer's mouth, while divine guidance and misguidance bracket them. The focus clause therefore adjudicates effective guidance: a claimed guide can name a path yet cannot make it traversable when divine misguidance has taken effect.

activation_trace.role: Guidance as indication toward road and truth is the efficacy denied to every would-be guide.
The prior divine negation makes guidance depend on more than a human claim to know a road.
Pharaoh appropriates the language of indicating a true road for his own asserted leadership.
The extended walkable road gives Pharaoh's claim a concrete route rather than abstract advice.
Straight guidance away from error is the destination Pharaoh claims for his route.
The repeated causative misguidance immediately after the focus confirms that deviation can defeat asserted direction.
The believer repeats the same guiding function but couples it to following rather than coercive assertion.
The same walkable-road image makes the two rival claims formally comparable.
Right direction names the shared claimed endpoint while leaving the claims' efficacy unequal.

structural_cues: 40:29 and 40:38 repeat أَهْدِيكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ with different speakers on opposite sides of the focus.
40:28 negates divine guidance for a prodigal liar, and 40:34 repeats the focus's divine causative misguidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies paired human guide claims plus divine guidance and misguidance; I infer that 40:33 revokes the performative efficacy of rival guide claims, while the live alternative is that it states a general maxim without adjudicating those speeches.

changed_reading.before: No guide means that nobody will offer correct directions.
changed_reading.after: Many voices can still claim the path of right, but no claimant can convert speech into an effective road for one whom God has caused to stray.

context_deltas.mechanism: A near-verbal echo denies any warder against God, yet refuge in God and entrusting the affair to God are followed by God's protection. The negation is directional rather than an absolute denial of protection: no independent shield can interpose against God, while protection can occur by reorientation into God's keeping.

activation_trace.role: Protective holding is the focus function whose source and direction the context clarifies.
The warding of harm appears in a close negated echo: no warder from or against God.
Seeking refuge and protective attachment supplies the positive orientation into divine shelter.
Aid that makes its recipient prevail sharpens the question of who could help against God's force.
Returning one's affair to another in reliance supplies the relational act preceding protection.
God's actual warding of harm shows that the surah does not deny protection in every relation.

structural_cues: 40:21 ما كان لهم من الله من واق closely anticipates 40:33 ما لكم من الله من عاصم.
The sequence 40:44-45 moves directly from entrusting the affair to God to God's protection from plotted harms.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the negated warder, refuge, entrustment, and subsequent protection; I infer that مِنَ اللَّهِ is oriented against divine action and that safety is available only within divine keeping, while the live alternative reads it simply as source and keeps the protected believer as a different case.

changed_reading.before: The ayah declares an absolute absence of any protector.
changed_reading.after: The ayah denies an autonomous shield against God; its sharper contrast is between futile protection from God and effective refuge in God's keeping.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding 'day of calling' makes the focus day acoustic and public. Its next action is back-turning, and later calls are characterized as lost, so the rout becomes a collapse of addressability: calls circulate, but no answering guide can orient the fugitives.

activation_trace.role: The severe-event day receives its acoustic and public specification from the preceding calling.
Turning away becomes the failed response made to the surrounding calls.
Raised voice and calling make the day an active field of summons rather than silent panic.
The gathering-place branch adds a public social field in which the calls and retreat are exposed.
Calling that seeks to incline an addressee supplies the response-demand whose efficacy later fails.
Loss gives the disbelievers' call the status of an address that cannot reach an effective destination.

structural_cues: 40:32 يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ is followed immediately by 40:33 يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ, allowing the second day-clause to elaborate the first.
The repeated مِنْ negations leave both protective and guiding response roles unoccupied.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency between the day of calling and the day of retreat plus a later lost call; I infer a call-response mechanism, while the live alternative treats the two day-clauses as parallel descriptions and the later prayer as a separate scene.

changed_reading.before: The fugitives run in a chaotic but otherwise silent scene.
changed_reading.after: They turn away inside a public field of summons whose calls no longer secure either an answering protector or an orienting guide.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated causative misguidance is attached to exceeding limits and agitated doubt, then followed by sealing and being barred from the road. Misguidance thus reads as a stabilized feedback loop: prior excess and doubt are stamped into a disposition that reproduces further turning away.

activation_trace.role: Deviation from intended direction is the focus condition to be explained as process rather than label.
Immediate repetition keeps divine causative deviation active across the focus boundary.
Exceeding the limit supplies a prior trajectory that misguidance can stabilize.
Agitated doubt supplies the unstable cognition that becomes locked rather than resolved.
Stamping and sealing supplies the mechanism by which a repeated trajectory becomes fixed.
Diversion and turning away externalize the sealed disposition as blocked movement.
The walkable road supplies the route from which the subject is barred.

structural_cues: 40:34-37 sequences causative misguidance, prodigality and doubt, sealing, beautified action, and diversion from the path.
The focus's causative يُضْلِلِ and the later passive صُدَّ leave different grammatical views of the same blocked trajectory.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sequence and repeated turning vocabulary; I infer the arrow excess and doubt -> sealing -> self-reproducing diversion, while the live alternative takes sealing as a verdict on an already complete condition rather than its sustaining mechanism.

changed_reading.before: God's misguidance is a one-time displacement onto the wrong road.
changed_reading.after: Misguidance is a feedback lock in which exceeded limits and unresolved doubt become sealed into a disposition that keeps turning from the available road.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes a sought way out and an offered salvation from mere retreat, then places all subjects inside return to God and a fixed abode. Back-turning is therefore abundant motion without an exit: a real escape had the form of accepting the offered route, whereas fugitive motion after refusal remains enclosed by return.

activation_trace.role: Retreat supplies motion away from the immediate scene but not yet a destination outside it.
The end and outcome branch makes the direction of flight answerable to its eventual terminus.
Passing outside supplies the explicit but unanswered desire for an exit.
A traversable road turns the desired exit into a route problem.
Fixity and settlement give the afterlife abode the stable endpoint that flight cannot dissolve.
Salvation as separation supplies the real exit offered before the scene of failed flight.
Return to a place closes the imagined outside into which fugitives might flee.
Being brought back confirms return as the terminal direction of apparently outward motion.

structural_cues: 40:11 explicitly asks whether there is any path of exit, while 40:41 offers salvation as a competing destination.
40:43 and 40:77 repeat return to God after the focus's imagery of turning away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exit, salvation, settlement, and return language; I infer a closed movement topology in which rejected salvation converts later flight into return, while the live alternative keeps these as separate eschatological statements without a shared spatial mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Turning their backs is movement away and therefore at least an attempted escape.
changed_reading.after: Their retreat is motion inside a closed return: the offered escape was a prior reorientation, and back-turning after its refusal has no outside endpoint.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the material strap branch of ع ص م rather than only its dominant protective sense. It remains anchored in the focus noun عَاصِم and gains packet support from the later collar, linked chain, neck, and dragging sequence. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy that sharpens failed protection, not as a replacement lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: عَاصِمٍ as both protective holding and, through its branch inventory, a strap or handhold

activation_trace.role: A strap, rope, or prepared handhold materializes the absent means of protective attachment.
A collar that binds an organ supplies the punitive inverse of a safety attachment.
The neck locates the imposed attachment on the fleeing body.
Connected links turn attachment from a possible handhold into continuous restraint.
Dragging and extension convert self-directed flight into externally imposed transport.

changed_reading.before: There is no savior able to stop the punishment.
changed_reading.after: There is no protective tether to grasp; the only later attachment is its punitive inverse, a collar-and-chain system that drags the former fugitives.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates هَاد as a leader or vanguard and places that image against the salient backs of مُدْبِرِينَ. It remains directly anchored in two focus words and produces a coherent spatial mechanism. Downstream prose should qualify it as a secondary spatial overlay on moral guidance, not as the primary sense of هَاد.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: مُدْبِرِينَ paired with the negated هَاد

activation_trace.role: The visible backs establish the rearward pole of the fleeing formation.
A guide who advances at the front supplies the missing forward pole and leading line.

changed_reading.before: The fugitives lack someone who can tell them where to go.
changed_reading.after: The rout is spatially frontless: backs are everywhere, but no vanguard occupies the forward position that could turn a crowd into an oriented formation.

strongest_changes: The negated protector becomes directional: no shield can interpose against God, although protection in God's keeping remains live.
The negated guide adjudicates rival claims to the same path of right, distinguishing named routes from divinely effective guidance.
The day of calling, failed calls, sealed diversion, and final return turn flight into a collapse of response and route rather than locomotion alone.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet exposed a close no-warder echo, mirrored human guide claims, and a movement sequence from public calling and back-turning through blocked roads to return and forced dragging; these supported several coexisting changes without reducing the focus to one theme.
remaining_uncertainties: The directional reading of مِنَ اللَّهِ remains syntactically live beside a source reading.
The arrow from excess and doubt through sealing to repeated diversion is reader-supplied from sequence, not explicitly stated as a causal chain.
The tether and front-of-formation readings are branch-backed analogies and should remain secondary to the dominant protection and guidance senses.
